rationales: One mole of H₂SO₄ has a mass of 98 g; more precisely, its molar mass is 98 g mol⁻¹.
98 amu is the mass of one H₂SO₄ molecule, not its molar mass.
The value 9.8 is ten times too small.
9.8 amu is neither the molecular mass nor the molar mass of H₂SO₄.
Ca(OH)₂ solubility decreases as temperature rises.
KNO₃ solubility increases as temperature rises.
Li₂SO₄ solubility also decreases as temperature rises, so this is another correct option.
AgNO₃ solubility increases as temperature rises.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass of these gases and therefore diffuses fastest.
Helium is heavier than hydrogen, so it diffuses more slowly.
Chlorine is much heavier and diffuses more slowly.
Fluorine is heavier than hydrogen and helium, so it diffuses more slowly.
KCl solubility changes noticeably with temperature.
KNO₃ solubility increases substantially with temperature.
NaCl solubility changes very little with temperature.
NaNO₃ solubility increases considerably with temperature.
Butter is a colloidal emulsion, not a solid-in-solid solution.
Fog consists of liquid droplets dispersed in a gas.
Brass is an alloy with solid zinc dissolved in solid copper.
Cheese is a colloid, not a solid-in-solid solution.
A concentrated aqueous solution of NaCl is called brine.
A solution of KCl is not called brine.
A solution of KNO₃ is not called brine.
A solution of KBr is not called brine.
Carbon is not the standard lustrous non-metal in these choices.
Sulphur is generally dull rather than lustrous.
Phosphorus is generally not lustrous.
Iodine has a lustrous, metallic-looking surface.
Rutherford identified the hydrogen nucleus as the proton.
Bohr developed the model of the atom but did not discover the proton.
Goldstein observed canal rays, not the proton itself.
Thomson discovered the electron.
The long-form table’s periods, groups, and blocks reflect the elements’ electronic configurations.
Atomic number determines the order of elements, but electronic configuration explains the long-form arrangement.
Mendeleev’s postulate concerned periodicity by atomic mass, not the basis of the long form.
Atomic number sets the sequence, while electronic configuration is the direct basis for the long-form structure.
The fifth period contains more than 8 elements.
The fifth period contains 18 elements.
A period with 26 elements is not the fifth period.
The fifth period contains fewer than 32 elements.
Nitrogen in NH₃ has a complete octet.
Boron in BF₃ has only six electrons around it, making the molecule electron deficient.
Each nitrogen atom in N₂ has an octet through the triple bond.
Each oxygen atom in O₂ has an octet in its usual Lewis structure.
Cl₂ and O₂ have nonpolar covalent bonds between identical atoms.
N₂ has a nonpolar bond; although H₂O is polar, both molecules in the pair are not polar covalent.
H₂O has polar bonds, but C₂H₂ is generally treated as nonpolar at this level.
Both HCl and H₂O have polar covalent bonds.
O₃ contains three atoms and is triatomic.
H₂O contains three atoms and is triatomic.
CO₂ contains three atoms and is triatomic.
H₂ contains two atoms, so it is diatomic, not triatomic.
Deuterium oxide (D₂O) is called heavy water.
Light water is ordinary H₂O.
Soft water is water with low concentrations of calcium and magnesium ions.
Hard water contains appreciable dissolved calcium or magnesium salts.
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among the halogens listed.
Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine and iodine.
Bromine is more electronegative than iodine.
Iodine has the lowest electronegativity among the listed halogens.
